issue.title: Name clash in ngbDropdown between a template input variable and a public var of ngbDropdownToggle
issue.body:
### Bug description:

In the plunker, you'll see a "menu" rendered using `*ngFor` for a set of dropdowns. The problem is the choice of the name `dropdown` for the template input variable in the `*ngFor`. That `dropdown` appears to conflict with the public variable `dropdown` of ngbDropdownToggle, causing both cryptic errors in the console and broken dropdowns. If you change the var name in the ngFor to anything other than `dropdown`, it works fine. 

This showed up in a real project (it broke between Alpha 5 and 6), and was pretty unexpected and difficult do debug. It is a problem even if you don't try to use the `dropdown` from the for loop in the label inside of the ngbDropdownToggle. 

I'm not actually sure whether this counts as an ngBootstrap problem or an Angular bug, or neither. This could be fixed, in part, by prefixing the `dropdown` var in ngbDropdownToggle, but I'm not sure what is the best practice here. I've never heard a suggestion that we should prefix our own local vars in, for example, an *ngFor--I never would have thought that such a local var name was at risk of clashing with anything, which makes me wonder if this is some problem on Angular's end.
### Link to minimally-working plunker that reproduces the issue:

http://plnkr.co/edit/R0HJDJZd6DoZgmKTnz9f?p=preview
### Version of Angular, ng-bootstrap, and Bootstrap:

Angular: 2.0

ng-bootstrap: alpha 6

Bootstrap: 4.0.0 beta 4

body: Just for the record - I'm not trying to find contrived cases here - this is happening in real projects and was originally reported in https://github.com/ng-bootstrap/ng-bootstrap/issues/813
